$GRAB $500B Market Cap is Inevitable Long Term🧵

GrabStay-The Next High Margin Segment. No this is not the $500B main thread(will write that later), just a title where I can get your attention, to discuss this massive potential segment.

Grab Holdings Limited, Southeast Asia's AI SuperApp, has masterfully evolved from a ride-hailing upstart into a multifaceted ecosystem encompassing mobility, deliveries, financial services, advertising, Tourism, Dine-out and B2B Solution(GrabMap). With 2025 revenue on track for $3.4–$3.5b and adjusted EBITDA guidance raised to $460–$480 million but should hit above $500m

Grab's trajectory is undeniably robust. Yet, as the company aggressively pivots toward tourism, its "secret sauce" of ecosystem integration demands a bold next step: launching an @Airbnb -like peer-to-peer (P2P) accommodation listing platform is inevitable. 

This isn't mere speculation; it's a logical extension of Grab's 2025 strategy, capitalizing on Southeast Asia's (SEA) tourism super-cycle to unlock 30–50% revenue acceleration by FY2026. 

1. Grab's Aggressive Tourism Push: The Foundation for SuperApp Dominance

Grab's tourism ambitions are no side hustle, they're a core pillar of its "S.M.A.R.T" framework (Sustainability, Market Expansion, Affordability, Retention, Tech & Innovation), explicitly highlighted in Q2 2025 earnings and CEO Anthony Tan's interviews . SEA's tourism rebound is explosive: international arrivals hit 121.3 million in 2024 (up 13% YoY) and are projected to reach 152 million in 2025, surpassing pre-COVID peaks by 10–15% (will be 250m by 2030). This $500B+ market opportunity aligns perfectly with Grab's 75%+ mobility market share(soon to be 90-95%) across eight countries (Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia, etc.), where 1 in 2 tourists already rely on the app for rides and payments . With recent partnership with @Alipay 1.7B users, @KlookTravel , booking dot com are all the prep steps to jump to $ABNB like accommodation. 

2. Is Mike the Fortune Teller now? No, but here are the early evidences:

~Government Partnerships: Grab has inked deals with tourism authorities in Thailand (e.g., "Tiew Tua Thai Suk Kan Yai Wai Jai Grab" campaign with the Tourism Authority of Thailand), Vietnam (five-year MoU with the Vietnam Tourism Development Fund for digital transformation), Singapore (collaboration with the Singapore Tourism Board for visitor insights), and the Philippines (preferred partner for airport transfers and events). These extend to Malaysia, Indonesia, Cambodia, and Myanmar, with airport banners and dedicated pick-up zones at major hubs like Suvarnabhumi (Thailand) and Hanoi (Vietnam)

~Bundled Experiences: Tourists book rides, food delivery, attractions (via Klook integration), and events in one app. Q2 2025 saw mobility GMV surge 20% YoY to $5.0 billion, partly fueled by tourism surges from concerts and corporate events. It is only logical to add ABNB like service to continue the momentum for bundled experiences!

~Affordability Levers: Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) via GrabPay integrates with Klook for 0% interest installments on tours/hotels, targeting underbanked users (60%+ in Indonesia). This drove GrabFin revenue up 42% YoY to $92 million in Q2

~Grab's CFO Peter Oey has called tourism a "super-cycle driver," with H2 2025 expected to show "strong" results from these initiatives . Analysts like those at @Forbes  project this could push FY2026 revenue to $5–$6 billion (40–70% growth), but Airbnb-like listings would turbocharge it by filling the glaring gap in Grab's travel stack: accommodations.

3. Why Airbnb-Like Listings? A Natural, High-Margin SuperApp Evolution

Grab isn't starting from scratch, it's already dipping into accommodations via partnerships with Agoda and https://t.co/4Idu8QUMDM since 2019, offering exclusive rates and vouchers redeemable in-app . However, these are third-party OTAs (online travel agencies), limiting control, margins (Grab earns ~5–10% referral fees), and data ownership. An in-house P2P platform think Airbnb's model of user-generated listings for homes, apartments, or unique stays would transform Grab into a true end-to-end travel superapp. AI is doing most of the coding today, Grab would only need few months to push this function. 

An Inevitable Strategic Fit:

~Ecosystem Synergy: Imagine a tourist landing in Bangkok, booking a Grab ride from the airport, reserving a local host's condo via GrabStay (hypothetical name), and bundling it with Klook tickets, GrabFood delivery, and BNPL; all in one seamless flow. This "one-app convenience" boosts retention by 15–20%, per Grab's internal data 
, while cross-selling lifts average transaction value (ATV) by 3-4x ($50–200 for travel bundles vs. $10 rides) 

~Addressing Airbnb's SEA Weaknesses: Airbnb dominates globally but struggles regionally with high fees (14–20%) similar to $Uber struggle, inconsistent listings, and poor integration with local transport/payments. Grab's 46 million monthly transacting users (Q2 2025) and 75% market share position it to steal share, especially as Airbnb faces regulatory scrutiny in Indonesia and Thailand . P2P listings would empower Grab's 220,000+ active advertisers (up 31% YoY) to list properties, driving GrabAds revenue (up to 20x ROAS) 

~Inclusive Growth Model: Aligning with @AnthonyPY_Tan  's "secret sauce" of uplifting drivers/merchants, hosts ( expats or locals with spare rooms) could earn 15–30% more via premium bundles, mirroring EV driver incentives This taps SEA's "bottom of the pyramid" economy, where 60%+ are underbanked but tech-savvy. 

~ Tech-Enabled Differentiation: Leverage @OpenAI 's @ChatGPTapp  Plus integration (free trial for GrabUnlimited subscribers) for AI-powered recommendations (e.g., "pet-friendly stays near beaches") and dynamic pricing . Blockchain via Alipay+ ensures secure, instant settlements for cross-border bookings 

4. When? This is Low-Risk, High-Reward Inevitable Rollout

Grab could pilot in high-tourism hubs like Thailand (48M+ visitors expected in 2026) and Singapore by Q4 2025, scaling regionally by mid-2027 

~Onboarding: Use existing merchant tools ( self-serve platform) for hosts; AI for listing verification.
~Monetization: 8–12% take rate + upsell fees ($5 for priority airport transfers).
~Risk Mitigation: Start with verified GrabUnlimited users as hosts to ensure quality; partner with regulators for compliance ( Vietnam's digital tourism MoU) 

Conclusion:  If this is launched early or earlier, the path to average 40-50% revenue growth would be much sooner, further defending my bull case for long term $500B MC thread later.

Grab's trajectory as Southeast Asia's SuperApp titan is poised for a transformative leap with the launch of an Airbnb-like P2P accommodation platform, GrabStay, by 2026. This isn't a speculative pivot—it's the linchpin of Grab's aggressive tourism strategy, seamlessly weaving accommodations into its ecosystem of mobility, fintech, and deliveries. With 152 million tourists flooding SEA in 2025, Grab's 75% mobility dominance and partnerships with regional governments position it to create 10-15% of the $800B  accommodation TAM, potentially adding $1–$2B in revenue by FY2026.

Unlike competitors like Airbnb, Grab's integrated superapp, lower 8–12% fees, and Alipay+ blockchain payments offer unmatched convenience and affordability, resonating with SEA's 700 million users and underbanked hosts. Backed by CEO Anthony Tan's proven execution and Grab's regulatory savvy, GrabStay isn't just a logical next step; it's an inevitable game-changer, redefining travel in SEA and cementing Grab as the region's unrivaled Everything SuperApp Ecosystem. The tourism super-cycle is here, and Grab is ready to own it.

This is NOT Financial Advice!

Disclaimer: I do own large $GRAB position on Private and Public portoflio. I don't get paid from the company

$GRAB & Thinking Ahead (MTU)🧵

Grab Dine-Out and Free Grab Map(much more accurate than Google Map) in the SuperApp are some of the greatest enagement drivers for the coming quarters/years. But Grab is missing some features that could drives more eyes/users to its Ecosystem. WeChat has that core (text messaging, voice/video calls, and group chats) with very minimal ads to retain users' experience. So we must explore new creative features to acclerate Monthly Transacting Users!

I can think of 4 different new products that can boost 46m monthly transacting users to 10x. 

To be the "The Everyday Everything App", Grab has a lot of work to do so it can translate that value to me and other shareholders(Long term). 

Disclaimer: I just want to be wealthier!

1. @AnthonyPY_Tan already figured 1 out with @OpenAI  ChatGPT. ChatGPT search will allow SEA users to explore the world most advanced data, where it replicates conversational/user friendly experience. Think of this as AI friend/recommendation over the long term, where it knows everything about you such as prefered food/ride/payment/dine-out/travel. 

2. GrabChat, to make it even more sticky than Wechat, give GrabPoint depending on how often they use the App. Allow Users to do multi-guest Live to so they users can have their own creative space. Users can also send meal/ride/voucher/gift with just a click. It shouldnt restrict like Tiktok, and give users more freedom to be creative. This enhances stickiness to Grab SuperApp Ecosystem. Focus on HyperLocal trend like other segment, where Users feel intergrated culutrally. The key to win this is how to tie users in this feature closer to the Ecosystem. 

3. GrabReview, This has to be more fun and engaging, where users can write product review, post video about a service, or simply shares tips to get good deals. GrabReview shouldnt be seamless intergrated to GrabChat, where users can link/pull the reivew up as they talk in the groupchat/group video. This will drive group Dine-Out, Travel, Ride, and potentially adding partnership for ecommerce. Allow users in this segment to earn commission, and connect them to wholesales so they have their own little shop, the products/services they want to feature. This creates income opportunities and drive even more purchases to the SuperApp ecosystem. 

4. GrabPod, with on-demand podcasts/music on localized topics from love, comedy, work, movie, events or anything to users' demand. This feature will drive engagement to sell even more GrabAds, where users can listen when riding or drivers doing deliveries. This should be tailored  to "Hyperlocal & Cultural Curation". Monetization could be $3-$5/month to download, early access to creators' collabs, or a discounted deal only exclusive to this creator. Users can also buy vouchers/ride/food for their favorite creators. Creators can also send exclusive code that they collab with merchants to their listeners. 

The idea is to offer more fun features to drive engagement and increase more purchases(MTU) on the App(stickiness). @AnthonyPY_Tan said Grab has aggressively adopted AI across its operation. Grab Could easily integreate GitHub Copilot or Amazon CodeWhisper to speed up these new features' development. 

Higher MTU= 
~More $ from GrabAds
~More $ from GrabUnlimited
~More purchases on its Mobility/Delivery/Fin

Just some ideas. J-curve growth requires bold leadership. 

We will see. 

Not Financial Advice

最近推特的账号策略我越发搞不懂了，姐妹 @web3_honey 的推特账号近期不幸被封，失去了超过一半的粉丝。

我见证了她从上一轮NFT周期开始，帮助BAYC在日本建立第一个社群，再到参与Azuki、Doodles等知名项目的建设。这一路走来，她所付出的努力和坚持，累积到了10万+粉丝并且跃升成为日本头部kol，极其不易。

她始终敏锐地把握着行业脉搏，从NFT到GameFi，再到AI，持续为许多海外项目搭建进入日本社区的桥梁。从Matr1x项目开始，我认识到她已成为日本市场的关键人物，虽说那时候没有合作，但我已经能看到，全球每一场区块链大会：东京，首尔，新加坡，吉隆坡，曼谷，马尼拉，河内，巴黎，香港，台北等等你都能看到她标志性红色头发的身影。今年我开始为Freestyle Classic举办线下活动，每一场她都亲自到场支持。这背后是常人难以想象的奔波与坚持。

日本市场建立社区和品牌绝非易事，懂的人都懂这里的门道非常深。但一旦建立信任，其社区的忠诚度与回报是惊人的。举个例子，当年Matr1x Fire的NFT和代币价格下跌时，全球其他社区没有一个不是抱怨的，但唯有日本社区创作了一幅《海贼王》风格的海报，象征着“旗帜未倒”的精神，令我感怀至今。

今年8月webx期间，我在虎之门艾迪逊举办了一场晚宴，honey帮我联系了8家餐厅和场地，并且帮我邀请了非常多的海外来宾，包括本土的几位大kol。于此同时，帮助我们与@syfuofficial 建立了非常好的联系。为FreeStyle Classic 接下来在日本发行NFT打下了坚实的基础。我在想，如果没有她的帮助，我都会缺乏勇气在日本举办私人晚宴，因为大多本地人社恐不愿意聚会，加之口语问题，很难完全取得信任和合作机会。

这一刻我明白了日本市场的独特性与珍贵性。因此，我坚信，任何项目若想进军日本，都需要一位本土代表塑造初印象、打通关键环节。我强烈推荐Web3Honey作为大使、顾问或咨询伙伴，助力项目落地日本。

I genuinely don’t understand Twitter’s account policies lately. My Sis @web3honey recently had her account suspended and lost more than half of her followers—just like that.

I’ve watched her journey from the very beginning: helping BAYC build its first community in Japan, contributing to iconic projects like Azuki and Doodles, and steadily growing to over 100K followers to become a top KOL in Japan. The persistence and effort behind this are truly not easy.

She has always had a sharp sense for where the industry is heading—from NFTs to GameFi to AI—consistently acting as a bridge for international projects entering the Japanese community. Since the Matr1x project, I’ve seen her become a key figure in the Japanese market. Even though we hadn’t collaborated back then, everyone could spot her iconic red hair at blockchain conferences around the world: Tokyo, Seoul, Singapore, Kuala Lumpur, Bangkok, Manila, Hanoi, Paris, Hong Kong, Taipei… you name it. And this year, when I started organizing offline events for Freestyle Classic, she showed up to support me every single time. The energy and dedication behind that are beyond what most people realize.

Building a community and brand in Japan isn’t easy—those who’ve tried know how nuanced it is. But once you earn their trust, the loyalty and support you receive are incredible. Take Matr1x Fire, for example: when its NFT and token prices dropped, communities everywhere were filled with complaints—except in Japan. There, the community created a “One Piece”-themed poster symbolizing that “the flag never falls.” That left a deep impression on me, even to this day.

During WebX in August, I hosted a dinner at Toranomon Edition. Honey helped me scout and connect with 8 different venues and invited many overseas guests, including several major local KOLs. She also helped us build a solid relationship with @syfuofficial, laying a strong foundation for FreeStyle Classic’s upcoming NFT launch in Japan. Without her support, I wouldn’t have had the confidence to host a private dinner here—many locals tend to be reserved, and language barriers make it hard to quickly build trust and collaboration.

It was then that I truly understood what makes the Japanese market both unique and valuable. That’s why I firmly believe any project looking to enter Japan needs a local representative—someone who can shape that crucial first impression and open the right doors. I strongly recommend Web3Honey as an ambassador, advisor, or consultant to help bring projects successfully into Japan.
